title: The call from Mount Safa
hook: He climbed a hill and asked whether they'd believe him if he warned of an army behind it.

screens.text: **He climbed a small hill and called out to every clan in Makkah.** When they came, he asked whether they would believe him if he said an army was waiting behind that hill.

**Start with family.** After about three years of private calling, Allah told him to warn his nearest relatives [Q 26:214]. The early biographers say he first gathered his extended family for a meal to invite them [Qalam ep. 34].

options.feedback: Yes. His relatives came first. Then the whole city.
Not quite. The verse says "your closest kindred": his own family.
Not quite. Letters to kings came much later. First, he was told to warn his closest kindred.

screens.text: **On the hill of al-Safa.** He climbed al-Safa and called the clans of Quraysh by name. He asked if they'd believe him if he warned of an army behind the hill. They said they had never known him to lie [Bukhari 4770].
bubbles: Then he told them he was a warner, sent ahead of a severe punishment [Bukhari 4770].

screens.text: From a family meal to the whole city.

events.title: A command
events.text: Allah tells him to warn his nearest relatives [Q 26:214].

events.title: A family meal
events.text: He invites his extended family to eat and hear him, the early biographers say [Qalam ep. 34].

events.title: On al-Safa
events.text: He calls the clans of Quraysh by name, and they gather [Bukhari 4770].

events.title: Never known to lie
events.text: Even his opponents admit they have never known him to lie [Bukhari 4770].

events.title: The pressure turns harsh
events.text: Believers with no tribe to protect them are tortured [Ibn Majah 150].

screens.text: **His own uncle.** In front of everyone, his uncle Abu Lahab cursed him and asked if this was why he'd called them all. A whole surah, al-Masad, was revealed about Abu Lahab [Bukhari 4770].
bubbles: Not every relative turned on him. Another uncle, Abu Talib, kept protecting him for years [IslamQA 11575].

screens.prompt: Why did he begin by asking if they'd believe a warning about an army?

options.text: To remind them he had never lied to them
options.feedback: Right. They said so out loud. His honesty was the ground he stood on to deliver the message.

options.text: Because an army really was coming
options.feedback: Not quite. It was a question to make a point: they already trusted his word.
Not quite. He was reminding them of his truthfulness before telling them something hard to hear.

screens.text: **Honesty first.** Years of honesty meant even the Prophet's ﷺ opponents admitted he never lied. Your everyday honesty will speak for your faith long before your words do. {teen}If you're under 18, talk to {{mentor.name}} before telling your parents about Islam.{/teen}
bubbles: And when family turns harsh, the Qur'an still asks you to keep company with your parents kindly in this world [Q 31:15].

screens.situation: At a family barbecue, Tyler's uncle loudly mocks his new faith. A few relatives laugh. Tyler's face is burning.

options.text: Stay calm, answer briefly and kindly, and keep treating his uncle with respect
options.feedback: Yes. A calm answer keeps his dignity and the family's peace. His character can do the talking.

options.text: Fire back and embarrass his uncle in front of everyone
options.feedback: Not quite. Winning the moment can cost the relationship. Calm and kind is stronger.
Not quite. One hard moment doesn't have to end family ties. Talk it over with his mentor.

check.prompt: When he asked Quraysh if they'd believe his warning, what did they say?

options.text: That they had never known him to lie
options.feedback: Right. Even before they rejected the message, they admitted he was truthful [Bukhari 4770].

options.text: That he had lied to them before
options.feedback: Not quite. They said they had never known him to lie [Bukhari 4770].

check.prompt: Who was the first group he was told to warn?

options.feedback: Not quite. He was told to start with his closest kindred [Q 26:214].

aiContext:
**Lesson facts**
- Allah commanded him to warn his nearest relatives [Q 26:214].
- The early biographers say he gathered his extended family for a meal to invite them [Qalam ep. 34] (single source: keep it cautious; Qalam says about forty relatives, with the meal prepared by 'Ali).
- He climbed al-Safa, called the clans of Quraysh by name, and asked if they'd believe him if he warned of an army; they said they had never known him to lie; he said he was a warner before a severe punishment [Bukhari 4770].
- His uncle Abu Lahab cursed him in front of everyone, and Surah al-Masad was revealed about Abu Lahab [Bukhari 4770].

**Likely questions**
- *"What is Surah al-Masad about?"* It condemns Abu Lahab, one specific uncle who openly fought the message. Don't quote it. Make clear it is not a model for how a convert treats their own relatives: the Qur'an asks believers to keep company with parents kindly in this world, even when they disagree [Q 31:15] (Day 14, Day 65).
- *"How do I tell my family I'm Muslim?"* There's no rush and no single right way; choose a calm time, lead with what hasn't changed (love, respect), and expect questions. Day 4 and Day 14 cover it. Under-18s talk to the mentor before telling their parents.
- *"A relative mocks my faith."* Calm, brief, kind; don't retaliate; keep ties if it's safe. If there's danger, follow the safety rule.
- *"What does 'warner' mean?"* Someone who warns of consequences out of care, like a person shouting about a fire. The Qur'an also calls him a bringer of good news; keep to this lesson's sources.

**Escalate:** any family situation that becomes unsafe (safety rule, never only the imam queue); teens' questions about telling parents go to the mentor.

**Don't**
- Don't quote Surah 111, and never use Abu Lahab to describe a convert's family.
- Don't compare the convert's family or their faith to the idol-worshippers of Makkah.
- Don't push the convert to tell family before they're ready.
- Don't picture the Prophet ﷺ.
